extracted.intended_audience: journalism students, educators, media researchers, and newsroom practitioners interested in celebrity/entertainment coverage
extracted.subtask_description: Framework of newsworthiness criteria and story-treatment conventions used to select and produce celebrity/entertainment journalism across media. Covers subject-selection signals, stylistic/treatment choices, implicit drivers, critiques and defenses of the genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harcup-O'Neill category — Celebrity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stories concerning people who are already famous"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this category when the primary newsworthiness derives from the subject's existing fame rather than the intrinsic public policy or societal importance of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harcup-O'Neill category — Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stories concerning sex, showbusiness, human interest, animals, an unfolding drama, or offering opportunities for humorous treatment, entertaining photographs or witty headlines"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply where the content appeals through amusement, emotion, spectacle, or visual/humorous potential. Often overlaps with 'celebrity' items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — A-list celebrity event
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage justified by the involvement of an A-list celebrity (any event)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any event becomes newsworthy if the subject is an A-list celebrity; editors prioritize these subjects regardless of event gravity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — B-list scandal
rubrics_metrics.description: Scandal involving B-list figures that drives coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scandalous or salacious incidents among less-prominent celebrities are emphasized because scandal is a primary driver of audience interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Reality TV / influencer events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events tied to reality television personalities or social media influencers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes items emerging from reality programming or influencer culture; treated as culturally salient regardless of traditional fame metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Dating / relationship news
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories about romantic relationships, hookups, breakups, engagements, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship updates are high-value items for celebrity coverage, often foregrounded over other information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Birth / death / marriage / divorce of famous
rubrics_metrics.description: Major life events (births, deaths, marriages, divorces) involving famous people
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These life milestones are classic triggers for widespread coverage and often receive prominent placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Public meltdowns / arrests
rubrics_metrics.description: Public breakdowns, arrests or legal troubles involving celebrities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crisis or criminality in a celebrity's life functions as high-drama content that attracts attention and sustained coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Red carpet / event appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearances at premieres, award ceremonies, or other public events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual spectacle and fashion elements make such appearances staples of celebrity coverage, often driven by photography opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Social media drama
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts, statements, or controversies unfolding on social platforms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social media posts / feuds create immediate, shareable story hooks and can rapidly escalate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Cultural product launches
rubrics_metrics.description: Launches of music, film, books or other cultural products by celebrities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product releases provide legitimate news hooks while also supporting promotional coverage and reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Brand / endorsement changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in commercial affiliations, endorsements or brand deals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business/brand moves by celebrities are framed as newsworthy for commercial and cultural reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Political activity by celebrities
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrities engaging in political statements, endorsements, or activism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When celebrities act politically, their fame amplifies the political message; coverage often examines both message and messenger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject selection — Charitable / philanthropic activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity involvement in charity work, philanthropic events or benefit campaigns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philanthropy is covered both for its human-interest value and as reputation/brand content for the celebrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Personalized framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional close-up focus on the individual rather than structural context
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories are framed around personal details and emotional angles that create intimacy and identification with the celebrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Visual prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of paparazzi photos, red carpet images, and other strong visuals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High visual value (photos, fashion shots) is prioritized for placement and can determine whether a story runs; drives layout and click interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Quote-heavy reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying on celebrities' own words as primary content
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct quotes amplify authenticity and personality; coverage frequently foregrounds celebrity statements or social-media posts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Speculation tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Comfort with presenting gossip and conjecture as part of news coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gossip—sometimes framed as 'might' or 'reports suggest'—is tolerated more in celebrity coverage than in hard news, allowing inference where evidence is thin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Anonymous source acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of unnamed sources (e.g., 'friends say') to supply intimate details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymous attributions are commonly used to provide salacious or personal details while avoiding direct sourcing constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Body, fashion, appearance focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to bodies, clothing, looks, weight, age, surgery and related details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical appearance is a frequent organizing frame, especially for female subjects; often prioritized over substantive achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Family / relationship details
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage emphasizing family dynamics, partners, children and private relationships
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private life details are foregrounded to humanize, sensationalize or dramatize the celebrity's personal sphere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story treatment — Dramatic narrative structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Framing stories as unfolding dramas with conflict and resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative arcs (build-up, climax, fallout) are imposed to sustain audience engagement across updates and follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Fame level (A/B/C list)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject's relative fame tier determines intrinsic newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors implicitly grade celebrities (A-list highest) and prioritize coverage according to perceived tier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Audience identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which audiences can identify or relate to the celebrity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that enable parasocial identification (aspiration, empathy, schadenfreude) are more likely to be selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Photo availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of usable paparazzi or event photographs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability of compelling images often converts marginal events into publishable items due to layout and click incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Conflict / drama dimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of interpersonal conflict, scandal or tension
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict is treated as a core attractor; stories with obvious drama are privileged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Surprise factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Element of surprise or unexpected behavior by a famous person
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexpectedness increases salience and editorial appeal; deviations from persona are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Cultural moment alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: How well the story aligns with broader cultural conversations or moments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that tap into ongoing cultural debates or moments are framed as more meaningful or relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Social media trending signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the item is trending or viral on social platforms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social traction is used as an editorial cue to run or amplify coverage quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Relationship updates as signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequent editorial attention to couple news, breakups, and dating status changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship status functions as a steady supply of stories; editors monitor these for hooks and updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Body / appearance changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting on weight, aging, cosmetic surgery or other physical changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical change stories are treated as inherently newsworthy, often invoking moralizing or voyeuristic tones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Personal life revelations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exposure of private details that reveal new aspects of a celebrity's life
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revelations (confessions, admissions, leaks) are prioritized as they provide novelty and intimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Brand / product tie-ins
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections between celebrity actions and commercial products or endorsements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial linkages legitimize coverage for business-news angles and advertorial synergy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit criterion — Political / activist statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity engagement in political speech or activism as a news trigger
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political activity by celebrities is covered both as politics and as personality-driven content, often emphasizing reaction over policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation — Crowding out substantive news
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity coverage can displace reporting on more substantive public-interest topics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this criterion to judge the opportunity cost of running celebrity items versus investigative or policy reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation — Personalization of systemic issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to reduce complex issues to individual personalities rather than structural analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether coverage personalizes broader social or political problems and thereby obscures systemic causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation — Reinforcement of gender stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that focuses women's bodies and appearance, reinforcing stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate gendered bias in story selection and treatment, especially disproportionate focus on women's looks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation — Encouragement of parasocial relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage that fosters one-sided, intimate fan-celebrity relationships
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ethical and social consequences of promoting parasocial bonds (privacy invasion, unrealistic expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical evaluation — Ethical concerns (privacy, mental health)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risks to celebrities' privacy and mental wellbeing arising from intrusive coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh public-interest justification against harms such as stalking, harassment or exacerbation of mental-health struggles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive evaluation — Mass audience reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrity journalism's ability to attract and reach large audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifies coverage on grounds of audience demand and the medium's sustainability; useful when weighing editorial priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive evaluation — Cultural significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that celebrity stories reflect meaningful cultural phenomena rather than triviality
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when assessing whether a celebrity item speaks to wider cultural trends or values beyond mere gossip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive evaluation — Celebrities as public figures
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim that celebrities are public figures with reduced privacy expectations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames invasive coverage as more permissible under the public-figure doctrine, though ethical limits still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defensive evaluation — Reflection of audience interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage justified by demonstrable audience interest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions may be validated by metrics of engagement and reader/viewer demand.
